transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess… I just haven’t been feeling like myself lately. It’s probably not as bad as it sounds, but I’ve gotten real quiet, don’t talk to people much, and I kind of go flat. Even starting my cleaning route at work feels harder than it should, like I’m pushing a loaded cart uphill. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you been feeling down or depressed?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but since the move it’s kind of been there most of the time—like a heaviness in the background. Low energy, not really enjoying much, feeling guilty about things I probably shouldn’t… even on days when other worries were taking up more space in my head, that sad feeling was still sort of underneath it. Is that… is that the kind of depressed you mean?
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah… I guess I have, though I don’t want to overstate it. I used to look forward to fishing on Saturdays, doing a crossword with my coffee, little things like that. Even at work, showing the younger guys a trick for stripping a floor used to feel kind of good. Lately I mostly just let those things sit, like they don’t really give me much back anymore. Is that what you mean?
Have you been feeling this depressed nearly every day for at least two weeks?

Yeah… I’d say so. I mean, not every minute of every day, but it’s been there pretty much nearly every day. It started not long after I moved, and that was… about a year and two months ago now. I probably should’ve said something sooner, I guess.
During this past year or so, was there ever a stretch of two months or longer when you were not feeling depressed?

No… I don’t think so. I mean, I had better days here and there, sure, but not a whole two months where it really lifted. It’s been kind of hanging around since not long after the move, so… about a year and two months now. Does that answer it right?
Did these feelings start because of the move?

I don’t know if I’d say the move caused it exactly… I don’t want to blame it all on that. But it did start not too long after I moved, and it’s kind of been with me since then — about a year and two months now. So the timing lines up, I guess.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot more than usual?
I’m not sure… I mean, I worry some, like anybody would, I guess. I haven’t really noticed it being a lot more than usual, but maybe I’m not the best judge of that. What do you mean by worrying a lot?
When you start worrying, is it hard to stop or control the worry?

I don’t know that it’s… out of control, exactly. Sometimes I can set it aside if I get busy with something. Other times it kind of keeps circling for a while, but I’m not sure if that’s more than normal. Does that make sense?
Before you moved, had you already been feeling depressed like this?

No, not really like this before. I mean, I’d had down days, sure, but this… this started after the move, not long after. It’s been hanging around since then, about a year and two months. I hope that answers what you mean.
Has this low mood lasted for 2 years or more?

No, not two years. It’s been… about a year and a couple months, I think. It started not long after I moved, and it’s kind of been there since then. So, around a year and two months—if that’s the kind of time frame you mean.
Do these feelings seem stronger than you’d expect from the move and what came with it?

I’m not totally sure. I mean, moving is a big thing, and I don’t want to make it sound more dramatic than it is. Some days it feels like maybe I should’ve adjusted better by now, but I don’t know what’s “expected,” exactly. Does that make sense?
Have these feelings been making it hard for you to function in your day-to-day life?

Yeah… I mean, I’ve been trying to keep it together, but it has made things harder. At work my supervisor started writing me up for missing routes and making the same cleaning mistakes, which is embarrassing to say. I used to be pretty steady with my routine.

And outside work, I kind of fell off from church, fishing, and checking in on people like I used to. I finally went to the employee assistance program because I just couldn’t keep my work routine straight anymore. I don’t know if that’s the kind of thing you mean.
If the move had not happened, do you think you would still have become depressed like this?

I’m not really sure, honestly. I keep going back and forth on that. Part of me thinks the move set a lot of this off, but… I can’t say for certain that I would’ve been fine if it hadn’t happened.

I don’t want to guess wrong. I just know it’s been since around then that I started feeling this way.
Have you noticed a change in your appetite?

Yeah… a little, I guess. I don’t want to make too much of it, but most days food just doesn’t really taste like anything—kind of like cardboard. So I’ll skip meals, or after my shift I might just eat a few crackers and call it good.

And, um… my work pants have been hanging looser than they used to. I don’t know if that’s helpful to mention.
Have you had thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of killing yourself?

I… I don’t have, like, some big plan or anything. I don’t want you to think I’m trying to be dramatic.

But a lot of mornings, I wake up and the thought is there that maybe it’d be easier if I just didn’t wake up at all. And… that scares me enough that I figured I should say it out loud.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that right. I mean… I haven’t really been keeping track of it.

Some nights are fine, I think, and other nights I’m just kind of lying there longer than I’d like. But I don’t know if it’s bad enough to call it trouble sleeping. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do your symptoms feel stronger than you would expect from the move?

I’m not sure, honestly. I keep thinking maybe the move explains it, and I don’t want to make it sound bigger than it is.

But… I guess I don’t really know what would be “normal” after moving. Some days it feels like more than just being unsettled, but maybe I’m not judging it right. Does that make sense?
Before this past year, was there ever another time in your life when you felt depressed like this for at least two weeks?

I’m not sure. I mean, I’ve had low stretches before, like anybody, I guess… but whether it was this kind of depressed and lasted two weeks, I don’t really know.

I don’t want to say yes if I’m remembering it wrong. Nothing is jumping out at me clearly, if that helps.
Do you feel your depression has been worse than you’d normally expect after a move?

I guess… I don’t know. I don’t want to overstate it.

A move is stressful, so part of me thinks, well, maybe this is just what happens. But it has felt heavier than I expected at times. I’m just not sure if I’m measuring that the right way. Does that answer it okay?
Before the move, was there ever a time in your life when you felt depressed or lost interest in things nearly every day for two weeks or longer?

I don’t think so… not that I can clearly point to. I’ve had times where I was down or not as interested in things, sure, but before the move I can’t really say it was nearly every day for two weeks or longer.

I don’t want to give you the wrong answer, but nothing specific comes to mind like that.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a first depressive episode beginning after a move, with persistent depressed mood and markedly reduced interest nearly every day for about 14 months, along with low energy, guilt, decreased appetite/weight loss, social withdrawal, occupational impairment, and passive death wishes. There is no clear evidence of prior depressive episodes, supporting a single depressive episode rather than recurrent depressive disorder. Although the move was a psychosocial stressor, the syndrome meets criteria for a depressive episode and has persisted far beyond the typical adjustment-disorder timeframe, making F32.9 more fitting than F43.23.
